The goal of mspcompiler is to offer ways to compile either EI or tandem mass spectral libraries from various sources such as NIST, MoNA, and GPNS.
NIST is the most commonly used commercial EI library.
Lib2NIST can be downloaded from https://chemdata.nist.gov/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=chemdata:nist17 if not installed with the NIST library.

For Agilent users, the NIST input file for Lib2NIST can be found in, for example, C:/database/NIST14.L. The NIST MS2 library input file for Lib2NIST can be found in C:/Programs/nist14/mssearch/nist_ms
The total number of spectra in a NIST library can be checked in the MS Search program under Options -> Libraries.
The *.MOL folder in NIST library export contains a large number of mol files and is time-consuming to move, copy, or delete.

The RIKEN EI library can be downloaded from http://prime.psc.riken.jp/compms/msdial/main.html#MSP. The RIKEN MS2 libraries can be downloaded from the MS-DIAL homepage at http://prime.psc.riken.jp/comp
The RIKEN EI library contains Kovats RI included.
The RIKEN EI library already has SMILES and InChIKey well-organized, so no further treatment is needed.
The MassBank of North America (MoNA) has an EI library available for download at https://mona.fiehnlab.ucdavis.edu/downloads.
The MoNA EI library file has SMILES information in the Comment field rather than the SMILES field.
The SMILES in MoNA EI library must be extracted from the Comment field and put into the SMILES field using the reorganize_mona function.
The Scientific Working Group for the Analysis of Seized Drugs (SWGDRUG) has compiled an EI library with drug or drug-related compounds.
The SWGDRUG library is available at https://swgdrug.org/ms.html.
To correctly parse the SWGDRUG library by mspcompiler, both NIST Format and Agilent Format downloads are required.
The SWGDRUG file does not contain InChIKey information.
Polarity options for assigning RI to combined EI libraries are semi-polar, non-polar, or polar.
Capillary GC columns are commonly used in the assign_ri function.
When there are multiple RI records for a single compound, the median RI will be used.
RI values with a standard deviation higher than 30 will be discarded.
Positive and negative modes in MS2 libraries are normally separated into 2 msp files.
The NIST MS2 exported msp file has both positive and negative modes mixed in a single file. Both positive and negative modes are in a single GNPS file.
The MoNA MS2 libraries can be downloaded from https://mona.fiehnlab.ucdavis.edu/downloads.
The GNPS library is organized in mgf format.
The GNPS library does not have the Molecular Formula (MF) field.
The molecular formula in GNPS library can be calculated from SMILES using the complete_mgf function.
The GNPS library can be downloaded from https://gnps.ucsd.edu/ProteoSAFe/libraries.jsp.
The read_multilibs function allows reading multiple msp files from a folder at once.
The mspcompiler package offers remove_ri and remove_rt functions to remove RI and RT respectively.
The change_meta function can be used to modify metadata such as comment, collision energy, and instrument type.
The RIKEN, MoNA, and GNPS MS2 libraries might contain identical spectra as they all compile some well-known libraries.
It takes a long time to process the NIST libraries.
Once NIST libraries are organized, they can be saved as .Rda files and reused in subsequent compilations.
Tandem mass spectral libraries are relatively big and consume high amounts of memory when read into R.
If a PC does not have enough memory, libraries can be processed separately and combined in a text editor like Notepad++.
The msp file is basically a text file.
